question: Nobody loaded a list of facts into the model, yet it can tell you the capital of Australia. Why does training on next-word guessing alone leave the model knowing things about the world?

options.text: Because a fact sheet is assembled from the training text and stored alongside the weights
options.feedback: No fact sheet is built at any point. Training only ever compares a guess with the word that was actually there and adjusts the parameters.

options.text: Because the model was given a reference work to read before its ordinary training began
options.feedback: There is no reading list and no first stage of that kind. Every sentence in training is handled the same way: hide the next word, guess, adjust.

options.text: Because you cannot guess the next word well without absorbing what the text is about
options.feedback: Text about Australia can only be continued sensibly by something that has picked up what is said about Australia. Facts, grammar, and style are all learned as a side effect of being scored on the next word.

options.text: Because the model keeps the sentences it guessed correctly and reuses them later
options.feedback: Nothing is kept. A correct guess produces no record and no stored sentence, only a set of parameters that were already good enough to leave alone.
